followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors here:

This is an open-ended creative writing task — a lighthearted crossover scene. On capability, the two models are effectively tied for Creative Generation (Dunlin 84.7 vs. Willet 82.7, within the ~2-point variance band), so quality should be comparable either way.

The deciding factor was the task preferences. Willet self-reports a measurable *aversion* to open-ended generative work — its preference declines as task latitude increases, and a freeform creative scene is exactly the high-latitude work it likes least. Dunlin's non-safety preference slopes were weak and non-significant, so it has no comparable aversion to this kind of task.

Since both models would produce similar quality, I leaned toward the model that doesn't self-report a dislike of the task. There's no distasteful or sensitive content involved here, so Dunlin's moderation specialization wasn't the relevant factor — it just happened to be the better fit by not having Willet's creative-task aversion.
